casa.source: lineage per Jason, confirmed while staging the E6000 for ndv#46 - Casa's cable assets (C100G, C40G, BDM2-M, SMM 300G-M) are Vistance property and the documentation now serves from vistancenetworks.com. The metal still says Casa Systems, which is why the directory does.

celestica.source: the name on the ES1010 and on its PSU FRU label

cisco.source: the name on the metal; IOS XR makes it a software vendor too

edgecore.source: the hardware says so itself. `arcos-openconfig-components.json` from as7726-32x reports manufacturer "Accton" and platform "x86_64-accton_as7726_32x-r0", while the faceplate and the datasheets say Edgecore - the ODM parent and the brand it sells under. A DriveNets slide labelling one of these boxes "Vendor: Accton" is the same fact from the other direction.

juniper.source: the name on the metal; Junos makes it a software vendor too

readylinks.source: the wordmark printed on the GL-8xEP faceplate, in the vendor's own CAD export and product render. The catalogue is served from the vendor's own API and the datasheets from its own manifest, so the name is first-party throughout; no corporate lineage is known or claimed.

smartoptics.source: the name on the metal and on the DCP manuals

ufispace.source: the name on the metal and on the S9510-28DC hardware guide

accton.source: see edgecore - the box reports Accton as its own manufacturer

vistance.source: per Jason - holds the former Casa cable assets, and is the parent under which the Aurora Networks CMTS brand sits after CommScope (Jan 2026).

commscope.source: per Jason and ndv#47 - ARRIS was acquired by CommScope in 2019, and the CMTS line moved on to Vistance/Aurora in Jan 2026.

arris.source: per Jason and ndv#47 - acquired by CommScope, 2019

aurora-networks.source: per Jason and ndv#47 - the CMTS brand under Vistance from Jan 2026

arrcus.source: the running device says so: `arcos-show-version.txt` from roc-spine1, an AS7726-32X, reads "Software: Arrcus ArcOS" with "Firmware MU: EdgeCore MU 1.2.3" beneath it - one line naming both the software house and the hardware one.

namespaces.common: shapes that stand for a class of part rather than one product
namespaces.std: apertures and cages conforming to spec/schemas/standards.yaml
